text:
Marathon Petroleum has climbed 7.81% over two weeks and edged up another 0.3% today as global refinery disruptions tighten diesel supplies and push prices higher. Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries and Iran sanctions are knocking offline major production capacity worldwide, while U.S. refineries are running at 98% utilization—near maximum—leaving little room to absorb supply shocks. Diesel has hit record highs as a result, which benefits refiners like Marathon by widening the margin between crude oil costs and the refined products they sell.

The broader picture is one of constrained supply meeting steady demand: crude inventories sit at 711 million barrels while diesel stocks have fallen to 104 million, signaling tight conditions. With geopolitical conflict disrupting refining capacity in Russia, Iran, and elsewhere, and the Strait of Hormuz (a critical oil chokepoint) potentially at risk, refiners have pricing power in the near term—exactly the environment that drives their profits higher.
